turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a, an and the?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Here is how I decide between a and an.
I have a pen. I ask myself: what is the first sound of "pen"? It is "p", not a vowel sound. So I use a.
That gives us the rule: a goes before other sounds, an goes before vowel sounds.
You can write "She eats an apple", but not "She eats a apple".

Now try the first exercise:
Write a or an: She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
turns.judgeInput:

Target form: articles. Learner level A2. First language Arabic.
W1 (wrong) strength 2: no a/an is needed before a singular noun. Its error: leaves out a/an ("She is teacher").
W2 (wrong) strength 1: a and an are the same; "a" (or "the") goes everywhere. Its error: uses "a" where "an" is needed ("a apple").
C1 (correct) strength 1: a singular countable noun needs a/an (or the). Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
